literal: Ruining and, to the ruined having become a support, again just like that uplifting and, all (is) rain.
translation: Rain is what ruins people by failing to fall, and rain is what uplifts the ruined by becoming their support.
modern: பெய்யாமல் மக்களைக் கெடுப்பதும், அவ்வாறு கெட்டவர்களுக்குத் துணையாக இருந்து மீண்டும் அவர்களை வாழவைப்பதும் ஆகிய எல்லாம் மழையே ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute power of rain over human prosperity. The word 'கெடுப்பதூஉம்' (ruining) refers to the devastation caused by droughts when rain fails. Conversely, 'எடுப்பதூஉம்' (uplifting) shows how the return of rain acts as a vital support to restore those very people. The elongated vowels in these two words are a poetic device (aḷapeṭai) that emphasizes the sheer magnitude of rain's dual capacity to both destroy and save.
